problem.name: Random spanning-tree sampling
problem.statement_latex: Given adjacency-list access to a connected graph $G=(V,E,w)$ with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and nonnegative finitely encoded weights, sample a tree with probability proportional to $\prod_{e\in T}w_e$, within total-variation error $\varepsilon$. Unit weights give the uniform spanning-tree distribution.

Unit weights give the uniform spanning-tree distribution.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(\sqrt{mn}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ time and adjacency-list queries by Apers--Gao--Ji--Liu. The quantum query lower bound is $\Omega(\sqrt{mn})$ at constant error.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(\sqrt{mn}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ time and adjacency-list queries by Apers–Gao–Ji–Liu. The quantum query lower bound is $\Omega(\sqrt{mn})$ at constant error.

classical.headline_latex: $O(m\log^2m)$ time at constant error by Anari--Liu--Oveis Gharan--Vinzant--Vuong's down-up-walk sampler, with logarithmic dependence on the target accuracy. The general weighted adjacency-list problem requires $\Omega(m)$ classical queries.
